text.p: Argentina's recently privatised oil company YPF is set to become a major beneficiary of long term oil price increases and is undervalued against its rivals, London-based brokers LatInvest said on Monday.

"YPF will be a prime beneficiary of a long term rise in oil prices, due to an expansion of oil production in Argentina and the restructuring at Maxus Energy," LatInvest said in a statement released in London.
U.S. oil company Maxus Energy Corp is owned by YPF.
"The company, however, remains undervalued against major international oil companies, the group it is generally benchmarked against," it said.
This was particularly clear on a price to cash flow basis, it said, while YPF ranks equal to or better than this group on an operating basis.
"The majors trade at more than seven times projected cash flow, while YPF trades at about four times projected cash flow," it added.

Some of the stock's overhang will be relieved by the Argentine government's recent statement that it intends to sell all or part of its remaining 20 percent stake, which may take place as a global offering or to a large industrial group, LatInvest said.
